title: GAO Prototype OTA Effectiveness and Transition Tracking Review
summary: GAO found that DOD could not systematically identify how often prototype OTAs became FAR production contracts and therefore could not fully assess whether prototype OTAs delivered capabilities.
key_findings: Fiscal 2024 prototype OTA obligations exceeded $16 billion.
DOD tracked production OTAs but lacked a reliable method to link prototype OTAs to follow-on FAR production contracts.
GAO made two recommendations and DOD agreed with both.
why_it_matters: The report establishes a system-level evidence gap between procurement mechanism and delivered capability, reinforcing the need for agreement-specific follow-through.
ftfn_relevance: Adds an independent oversight boundary to the OpenAI prototype trail.
Distinguishes individual award evidence from department-wide transition measurement.
evidence_limits: The report did not assess the OpenAI agreement and cannot establish its outcome.
